title: By myself
goal: Say myself, yourself and my own with öz, and follow a story told in the passive.

intro.text: *Öz* before a noun with a possessive means **own**: *öz öýüm* (my own house). With the possessive on itself it means **self**: *özüm* (myself), *özüň* (yourself), *özi* (himself, herself), in any case: *özüme* (for myself), *özüňi* (yourself, as an object).

vocab.en: to oneself, on one's own (öz-özünden: by itself)

exercises.question: How do you say **I did it myself**?

why.2: *Öz* on its own goes before a noun: *öz öýüm*. For **myself**: *özüm*.

exercises.label: *öz* with the possessive: myself, yourself…
exercises.explain: The possessive endings round after ö in the second syllable: *özüm, özüň*; at the end of the word, *özi*.

exercises.en: We live in our own house.
exercises.explain: Before a noun with a possessive, *öz* means **own** and takes no ending: *öz öýümiz*.

exercises.prompt: I bought myself a new shirt.

exercises.question: *Gapy öz-özünden açyldy.* What happened?
options: The door was opened by him.

why.1: **His own door** would be *öz gapysy*, with the active *açdy*.

exercises.explain: *Öz-özünden*: by itself, on its own; *açyldy*: opened, was opened.

exercises.prompt: The child got dressed by himself.
Look at yourself in the mirror!
exercises.explain: *seretmek* (to look at) takes the dative: *özüňe*, at yourself.

exercises.prompt: Bu halyny öz elim bilen dokadym.
accept: I wove this carpet with my own hands.
I wove this rug with my own hands.
I made this [carpet|rug] with my own hands.

exercises.question: Which sentence means **the carpet was sold**?

why.1: *Satdy* is active: the carpet would be the seller.
why.2: *Halyny satdy*: **he sold the carpet**, active, with an object.

exercises.explain: *özi* (herself) before the verb stresses that nobody helped.

exercises.title: Halyçy
exercises.passage:

exercises.translation: Bahar daýza lives in Mary province. She is a carpet weaver: she weaves carpets with her own hands. There is a big room in her house. This room is used only for weaving carpets. Every morning Bahar daýza has a wash, gets dressed and starts work. A carpet takes several months to weave. The patterns of the carpet aren't drawn on paper: Bahar daýza knows them by heart. Last year a carpet she wove was sent to an exhibition in Ashgabat and sold there. Bahar daýza was very happy. Now she is teaching her daughter to weave carpets too. Her daughter has started weaving her own first carpet.

questions.q: What is the big room used for?
options: for her daughter's lessons at school
questions.explain: *Bu otag diňe haly dokamak üçin ulanylýar.*

questions.q: Why aren't the patterns drawn on paper?
What happened to the carpet she wove last year?
options: it was sent to an exhibition in Ashgabat and sold
she gave it to her daughter
questions.explain: *Aşgabatdaky sergä iberildi we şol ýerde satyldy*: it was sent and sold, passive.
